page: Microsoft Azure L48ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance built on the arm64 processor architecture and deployed under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This balanced density between execution threads and physical memory accommodates substantial concurrent execution overhead.

The primary hardware differentiator of the L48ps_v5 is its massive direct-attached storage subsystem, which incorporates 11,519 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. The inclusion of integrated NVMe storage alongside Premium Storage capability delivers low physical access latencies and high input/output bandwidth, eliminating network storage transfer bottlenecks for data-heavy read and write operations.

Operating on an ARM-based compute tier allows the instance to achieve favorable operational efficiency and compute density relative to traditional x86 alternatives. Tradeoffs include the prerequisite for ARM-compatible application code and binaries, the absence of hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs, and zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, necessitating virtual network gateway planning for public accessibility.

Given its 11.5 TB local NVMe capacity and 384 GB memory allocation, the L48ps_v5 is technically suited for large distributed NoSQL databases, transactional data warehouses, search indexing clusters, and intensive ETL pipelines requiring rapid local scratch space and reliable memory-resident caching.
description: Microsoft Azure L48ps_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for I/O-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by an arm64 processor architecture within Microsoft Hyper-V, the configuration provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core allocation. A major technical asset is the bundled 11,519 GB local NVMe SSD array alongside Premium Storage support, granting direct access to low-latency, high-capacity solid-state storage without relying purely on network disk volumes. The ARM-based compute fabric offers notable resource efficiency and high compute density, though workloads must be verified for ARM instruction set compatibility. Because the instance omits discrete GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, it focuses squarely on dense compute, memory, and high-throughput local disk operations. The L48ps_v5 is particularly suited for large-scale relational and NoSQL databases, search indexing clusters, data warehousing nodes, and distributed file processing systems requiring massive high-speed ephemeral or scratch storage.
